rules.heading: Write forward-only numbered idempotent migrations, each opening with what and why
rules.evidence: Nothing in the harness fact set touches schema migrations, ledger tables, filename ordering, or baseline dumps; the closest native instruction surface is CLAUDE.md, which is explicitly advisory context rather than any migration mechanism.

rules.heading: Back up before a destructive migration, and diff after it
rules.nativeFeature: Checkpointing limitation — Bash-modified files untracked (and checkpointing is not a replacement for version control)
rules.evidence: The harness's own undo path stops well short of this rule: checkpointing "does not track files modified by bash commands such as rm, mv, or cp" and is documented as "designed for quick, session-level recovery" rather than durable history, so nothing in the session can restore a dropped table.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: none, because the backup lands outside the repo and the session cannot restore it either: checkpoints do not track what a Bash command changed and are not a substitute for version control, so the runbook step and the pasted post-migration diff are the control.

rules.heading: Treat provenance columns as behavior
rules.evidence: No fact in the harness set concerns row provenance, sync writers, or column ownership in a database; the harness's only memory-of-origin concept is auto memory's frontmatter type field, which records why Claude saved a note and has no bearing on stored rows.

rules.heading: Let row lifecycle decide a new table, never ownership
rules.evidence: Table grain, row churn, and column-scoped grants have no counterpart anywhere in the harness facts, which cover instruction files, permissions, plugins, sessions, and subagents only.

rules.heading: Add the table registry line in the same PR as the migration
rules.nativeFeature: Hosted Code Review CLAUDE.md customization, plus the Code Review check run that never blocks merge
rules.evidence: Hosted Code Review does notice documentation drift, since "if your PR changes code in a way that makes a CLAUDE.md statement outdated, Claude flags that the docs need updating too," but it surfaces that only as a nit-level finding and "the check run always completes with a neutral conclusion so it never blocks merging," and it is unavailable to orgs outside Team or Enterprise.
rules.proposedWording: Anchor: a schema invariant that fails on an unregistered table and on a stale registry line, run before any publish or deploy, because the hosted review that notices a doc going stale raises it as a non-blocking nit and is not available in every org.

rules.heading: Store money as integer cents and reconcile against the books
rules.evidence: Column types, provider fee records, and external-statement reconciliation appear nowhere in the harness facts; the only native cost surface is Claude Code's own token spend reporting, which is unrelated to stored money columns.

rules.heading: Give each initiative its own least-privilege role
rules.nativeFeature: Read/Edit path rule enforcement scope, plus Sandbox scope (tools and processes it does not cover)
rules.evidence: The harness enforces at the tool boundary and stops there: deny rules "apply only to Claude's built-in file tools and Bash file commands it recognizes, NOT to arbitrary subprocesses that read/write files themselves," and the sandbox "isolates Bash subprocesses only," so neither can see a query a running pipeline issues against a sensitive table.
rules.proposedWording: Enforce the firewall with a runtime guard and not only with a grant whenever the build itself runs as a privileged role, since a grant that permits the read cannot stop it and the harness stops at the tool boundary: permission rules and the sandbox never reach inside a script's own database queries.

rules.heading: Never let a write script pick its target from a dotfile
rules.nativeFeature: Bash wildcard rule matching, plus the fixed list of Bash command wrappers stripped before matching
rules.evidence: The permission layer matches command text and nothing beyond it, and the docs warn that argument-constraining Bash patterns are "fragile, bypassable via option ordering, protocol changes, redirects, variables, or extra spaces," while environment runners such as direnv exec are not in the stripped-wrapper list, so no rule can tell which database a run resolves to.
rules.proposedWording: Read the connection string for any write path from the exported environment, never from a dotfile some tool loads on your behalf, because permission rules match only the command text and cannot see which database a run resolves to, and an environment runner like direnv is not stripped before that match.

notes:
Whole-file read at plugins/house/modules/database/rules/database.md; eight "## " headings plus "## Don't", which I excluded per instructions. No rule in this file is a DUPLICATE or a CONFLICT: the harness fact set has no database surface at all, so nothing here restates or fights a native mechanism.

Rules I was unsure about, all three on the COMPLEMENT versus UNIQUE line rather than on substance:

- "Back up before a destructive migration, and diff after it": the subject matter (database backups) is entirely outside the harness, which argues UNIQUE. I called it COMPLEMENT because the checkpointing facts state plainly that bash-driven changes are untracked and that checkpoints are not version control, and a reader who assumes /rewind covers a destructive run is exactly the reader this rule needs to reach. If the owner reads a native cite here as reaching too far, downgrade to UNIQUE and keep the anchor line as written.

- "Add the table registry line in the same PR as the migration": hosted Code Review's bidirectional doc-staleness check is genuinely adjacent, but it is nit-level, non-blocking, and Team/Enterprise research-preview only. That combination is what makes the cite worth adding rather than a reason to delete the rule. The risk is that adopters without Code Review find the cite irrelevant, so the proposed wording names the floor as a reason for the invariant rather than as a dependency.

- "Never let a write script pick its target from a dotfile": the direnv-not-stripped fact is a strong match for the dotfile-loader failure shape, but the rule's real subject is process discipline in the app's own code, not permission-rule design. I judged the cite worth making because it explains why no allowlist can substitute for the fail-fast check. UNIQUE would also be defensible.

The four keeps (migrations, provenance, row lifecycle, money) are clean UNIQUE calls with no near-miss native feature worth naming.
